clue.text: Turn bad and get extra benefit

parts.note: a spin is a turn or rotation
food that has gone bad is off

explanation.surface: Something that goes wrong somehow ends up paying out a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-product that brings an unplanned additional advantage is a familiar business term for incidental gain.

clue.text: Wearing a vest? The only one in a suit, too

definitions.text: The only one in a suit

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
having clothes on means wearing them

explanation.surface: Only one person in a suit, while everyone else is in their undershirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing a vest is read as 'singlet on'. In card games, a lone card of a suit in a hand is so called; in Britain a vest is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a singleton is a holding of just one card in a particular suit, the lone member.

clue.text: It may be raining, so use a fast-colour dye

indicators.note: may be suggests the answer could be a rearranged version of the given word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rain is coming, so pick a dye that won't run.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingrain originally meant to dye in grain, fixing a colour fast in the fibre before weaving.

clue.text: Abroad, mechanic needed person to supply gear

parts.note: out and abroad both mean away from home
a fitter is a mechanic who assembles machinery

explanation.surface: Overseas, a mechanic had to find someone to provide equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or trader who sells clothing and equipment, for expeditions or schools.

clue.text: Go on a strict diet with all speed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to go without food

explanation.surface: Someone starts a severe diet in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to abstain from eating and, as an adverb, rapidly or swiftly.

clue.text: Huge swimmer taking a little drink put back on weight

parts.note: a gram is a unit of weight

indicators.note: putting something back sends it in the opposite direction, so the drink is read from right to left

parts.note: to sup is to take a small mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: A big swimmer has a drink and promptly puts the weight back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means the reversed drink follows the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A grampus is a large dolphin-like sea mammal, Risso's dolphin or the killer whale, so a huge creature of the sea.

clue.text: Bland nature of grub the head offered

parts.note: a gentle is an old word for a maggot used as fishing bait
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: The headteacher served up tasteless food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food; it is the larva. 'Head' is a headland, not a headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentleness is a mild, soft and kind disposition, which bland, in its sense of mild and unprovocative, describes.

clue.text: Lively Anglo-French articles about American fighter

indicators.note: about means the two articles go round the soldier

parts.note: the English article A and the French article LE
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Lively reports on a US fighter written in English and French.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and quick in movement, so full of life and energy.

clue.text: A game of bridge

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the card game also known as twenty-one or blackjack
second meaning: a floating bridge supported on boats

explanation.walkthrough: 'A game of bridge' reads as one card game; split it into a different card game and a kind of bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a card game played to reach twenty-one, and a temporary floating bridge resting on boats.

clue.text: Shabby, like the nursery beds?

definitions.note: adjective describing beds full of seed
definitions.meaning: second meaning: full of seed, as beds in a plant nursery are

explanation.surface: Children's beds in a nursery are looking rather worn.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery is a plant nursery, not a children's room.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sordid or run-down, and literally full of seeds, as freshly sown beds would be.

clue.text: Strange thing to say in brief retirement speech

definitions.text: Strange thing to say in brief retirement speech

parts.words: Strange thing to say in brief retirement speech
parts.note: surface reading: an odd remark in a short speech on leaving a job
setter's reading: retiring means going to bed, and the brief speech is the clipped form of a bedtime farewell

explanation.surface: Someone says something odd in a short farewell speech at their retirement party.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is going to bed, not leaving work; the word is what is left when 'good' is dropped from the bedtime goodbye, an odd thing to say on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: People heading off to bed often say just the clipped farewell, a shortened version of the usual goodnight wish.

clue.text: Feeling fine, say, around one

indicators.note: around says the punishment word wraps itself about the numeral for one

parts.note: a fine is an example of a sentence passed by a court, hence 'say'
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone reports feeling fine, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feeling fine' reads as a phrase about health; 'fine' is the court penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to perceive and experience sensations, which is what feeling as a noun describes.

clue.text: An idle eccentric provides the introduction

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the letters are set in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lazy oddball is the one who gets the opening remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead-in is the opening passage or remarks that introduce a programme, speech or piece of writing.

clue.text: Making each and every point with bloody fable!

parts.note: all covers each and every one
E for east, a compass point
gory means covered in blood

explanation.surface: A storyteller gets every point across with a gruesome tale.
explanation.walkthrough: E is a compass point, east.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story with a hidden moral meaning, much like a fable that teaches a lesson through its characters.

clue.text: At the same time, he's a learner

definitions.text: At the same time, he's a learner

parts.words: At the same time, he's a learner
parts.note: surface reading: someone is a student while doing something else
setter's reading: he studies at the same place and the same time as you

explanation.surface: Someone is learning while also doing something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the same time' looks like 'meanwhile'; it means alongside you in class.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow pupil attending the same institution during the same years is a classmate in education.

clue.text: Principle that might just as well be reversed

indicators.text: might just as well be reversed
indicators.note: if turning the word round makes no difference, it reads identically in both directions

parts.note: a word for a principle that reads the same either way

explanation.surface: A rule of belief so flimsy it could be flipped without anyone noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is also the wordplay source: the principle-word reads identically backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, a guiding principle of a person or group.

clue.text: A woman not in favour of attitude taken by body

parts.note: con as in pros and cons: against
a stance is a bodily posture, and also an attitude

explanation.surface: A woman disapproves of the posture someone has adopted.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a female given name, so it serves as an example of a woman.

clue.text: Clement, exhibiting some impatience, scoffed

parts.note: a temper is a fit of irritation
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A man called Clement showed a flash of impatience and mocked someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement looks like a man's name and 'scoffed' like jeered; in Britain to scoff food is to wolf it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild, and temperate means mild in climate, free of extremes.

clue.text: Oriental flier accompanied by a partner always

parts.note: E for eastern
a tern is a seabird
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: An Eastern pilot always flies with a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means forever, at all times without end, the same as always.

clue.text: Taking no nonsense over financial liabilities — famed for it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down-or-back sense, turned over means the nonsense word is read backwards

parts.note: rot is rubbish or nonsense
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: A firm stance against nonsense about debts earns someone a reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famed for it' carries a sly hint of bad fame, which is just what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means widely known, usually for something bad, so famous for the wrong reasons.

clue.text: Checking out and setting off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone checks out of a hotel and sets off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting off' reads as departing; it is the instruction to scramble a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing is examining something to check whether it works or is right, which checking out means.

clue.text: Doctor a mineral for poet

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer
ore is a mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: An instruction to tamper with a mineral sample for a poet's benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a verb meaning tamper with; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Moore was an Irish poet and songwriter, author of the Irish Melodies and Lalla Rookh.

clue.text: General left front of army lines

parts.note: left over: remaining

indicators.note: front of points to the opening letter of the following word only

parts.note: the first letter of army
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A general leaves the front line of an army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall means taking everything into account, comprehensive, which is general in its sense of broad.

clue.text: Taps out sick-note, giving throat-lozenge, perhaps

indicators.note: out suggests disorder or being put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ill means sick
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A sick note from the doctor comes with a cough sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick-note' looks like one item, but splits into sick and a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small medicated sweet sucked to soothe the throat; a lozenge is one example.

clue.text: Took steps to move stuff outside the church

indicators.note: outside puts the stuffing word on both sides of the church abbreviation

parts.note: to pad is to stuff with soft material
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone acted to shift a load of things out of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To pace is to walk with steady strides, so taking steps in order to move along.

clue.text: State of house under princess

indicators.note: in a down entry, under puts the house abbreviation below the princess, so it comes second

parts.note: Princess Ida is the Gilbert and Sullivan heroine
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: The condition of a house beneath a princess's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' in a down clue puts house below princess; 'State' reads as a condition, but is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the north-west of the country.

clue.text: That woman takes an age to get on this

parts.note: her refers to that woman
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: A woman spends forever getting on with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereon is a formal adverb meaning upon this or following on from this point.

clue.text: Leading man in the romance?

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Who plays the male lead in a love story?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the romance both hides and fits the leading man.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero is the principal male character of a story, the leading man of a play or film.

clue.text: Cups, possibly, as result of showing backbone about a contest

indicators.note: about places the backbone word around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a chine is an animal's backbone
taken as written
a war is a contest between forces

explanation.surface: Winning trophy cups is the reward for showing spine in a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: Cups suggests sporting trophies; here they are crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinaware is porcelain tableware, and cups are an example of it.

clue.text: A number of Romans are in poor shape, but help is here

parts.note: A taken as written, plus V, the Roman numeral five
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Some Romans are in a bad way, but rescue has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or benefit, as in 'of no avail', so assistance.

clue.text: Moved up following a hound — such a bloomer!

indicators.note: following means the moved-up word comes after the hound, so it is placed second

parts.note: a hound is a dog
rose means went up

explanation.surface: Someone climbed after a hunting dog, and what a blunder that was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the moved-up word after the hound. A bloomer is British slang for a blunder; here it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog rose is a wild climbing rose of hedgerows, so a plant that blooms, a flowering thing.

clue.text: Too unprofessional to cover up

parts.note: over as in over-eager means too
lay people are not of a profession

explanation.surface: Someone is too amateurish to hide their mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlay is to spread something on top of a surface so as to conceal or coat it.
